Every core `airflow` command: 26 top-level commands and groups, 99 commands in all. Most of them read the metadata database directly, so run them where the scheduler's configuration and database access are available, or use the REST API and `airflowctl` instead ([REST API and airflowctl](05_rest_api_and_airflowctl.md)).

Executors and auth managers from providers add more groups at run time, for example `airflow celery` (Celery provider), `airflow kubernetes` (cncf.kubernetes provider) and `airflow users` / `airflow roles` (FAB auth manager). Those come from the providers and are not listed here; run `airflow <group> --help` in your deployment.

Every command also accepts `-h` / `--help`.

## airflow api-server

Start an Airflow API server instance

```text
airflow api-server [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `-p`, `--port` | The port on which to run the API server | `conf.get('api', 'port')` |
| `-w`, `--workers` | Number of workers to run on the API server | `conf.get('api', 'workers')` |
| `-t`, `--worker-timeout` | The timeout for waiting on API server workers | `120` |
| `-H`, `--host` | Set the host on which to run the API server | `conf.get('api', 'host')` |
| `--pid` | PID file location |  |
| `-D`, `--daemon` | Daemonize instead of running in the foreground | flag |
| `--stdout` | Redirect stdout to this file |  |
| `--stderr` | Redirect stderr to this file |  |
| `--log-config` | (Optional) Path to the logging configuration file for the uvicorn server. If not set, the default uvicorn logging configuration will be used. | `conf.get('api', 'log_config', fallback=None)` |
| `--apps` | Applications to run (comma-separated). Default is all. Options: core, execution, all | `'all'` |
| `-l`, `--log-file` | Location of the log file |  |
| `--ssl-cert` | Path to the SSL certificate for the webserver | `conf.get('api', 'ssl_cert')` |
| `--ssl-key` | Path to the key to use with the SSL certificate | `conf.get('api', 'ssl_key')` |
| `--ssl-ca-file` | (Optional) Path to the SSL CA file | `conf.get('api', 'ssl_ca_file', fallback=None)` |
| `--ssl-cert-reqs` | (Optional) Set certificate verification options. Choices: `('none', 'optional', 'required')`. | `conf.get('api', 'ssl_cert_reqs', fallback='none')` |
| `--ssl-ciphers` | (Optional) OpenSSL cipher list to use when SSL is enabled. | `conf.get('api', 'ssl_ciphers', fallback='')` |
| `-d`, `--dev` | Start in development mode with hot-reload enabled | flag |
| `--proxy-headers` | Enable X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Port to populate remote address info. | flag |

## airflow backfill

Manage backfills

| Subcommand | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| [`create`](#airflow-backfill-create) | Create a backfill for a dag. |

### airflow backfill create

Run subsections of a Dag for a specified date range.

```text
airflow backfill create [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `--dag-id` | **Required.** The dag to backfill. |  |
| `--from-date` | **Required.** Backfill window start (inclusive). For partitioned Dags, this range is interpreted as the partition-date range (auto-detected). |  |
| `--to-date` | **Required.** Backfill window end (inclusive). For partitioned Dags, this range is interpreted as the partition-date range (auto-detected). |  |
| `--dag-run-conf` | JSON dag run configuration. |  |
| `--run-backwards` | If set, the backfill will run tasks from the most recent logical date first. Not supported if there are tasks that depend_on_past. | flag |
| `--max-active-runs` | Max active runs for this backfill. |  |
| `--reprocess-behavior` | Select which Dag runs to create: 'none' (Missing Runs), 'failed' (Missing and Errored Runs), or 'completed' (All Runs). Default is 'none'. Choices: `('none', 'failed', 'completed')`. |  |
| `--run-on-latest-version` | (Experimental) The backfill will run tasks using the latest bundle version instead of the version that was active when the original Dag run was created. If not specified, uses the DAG-level or global configuration default (falling back to True for backfills to preserve historical behavior). | `None` |
| `--dry-run` | Perform a dry run | flag |

### airflow connections export

All connections can be exported in STDOUT using the following command:
airflow connections export -
The file format can be determined by the provided file extension. E.g., The following command will export the connections in JSON format:
airflow connections export /tmp/connections.json
The --file-format parameter can be used to control the file format. E.g., the default format is JSON in STDOUT mode, which can be overridden using: 
airflow connections export - --file-format yaml
The --file-format parameter can also be used for the files, for example:
airflow connections export /tmp/connections --file-format json.
When exporting in `env` file format, you control whether URI format or JSON format is used to serialize the connection by passing `uri` or `json` with option `--serialization-format`.

```text
airflow connections export <file> [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `file` | Output file path for exporting the connections |  |
| `--format` | Deprecated -- use `--file-format` instead. File format to use for the export. Choices: `['json', 'yaml', 'env']`. |  |
| `--file-format` | File format for the export Choices: `['json', 'yaml', 'env']`. |  |
| `--serialization-format` | When exporting as `.env` format, defines how connections should be serialized. Default is `uri`. Choices: `['json', 'uri']`. |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

### airflow connections import

Connections can be imported from the output of the export command.
The filetype must by json, yaml or env and will be automatically inferred.

```text
airflow connections import <file> [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `file` | Import connections from a file |  |
| `--overwrite` | Overwrite existing entries if a conflict occurs | flag |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

### airflow dags clear

Clear Dag runs of the given dag_id and re-queue them for reprocessing. Exactly one of the following selectors must be provided: --run-id (single run); --partition-key (every run with that exact partition_key); or a partition_date window via --partition-date-start and/or --partition-date-end (both bounds are inclusive, interpreted in the Dag's timetable timezone). Intended for partitioned Dags, whose runs are keyed by partition_date / partition_key instead of logical_date. For traditional, non-partitioned Dags, use `airflow tasks clear --start-date / --end-date`.

```text
airflow dags clear <dag_id> [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `dag_id` | The id of the dag |  |
| `--run-id` | Clear the Dag run with this run_id. |  |
| `--partition-key` | Clear all Dag runs whose partition_key matches this exact value. |  |
| `--partition-date-start` | Inclusive lower bound of the partition_date window. The wall-clock value is re-interpreted in the Dag's timetable timezone. A date-only value (no time) is treated as local midnight. Accepts the same datetime formats as --start-date. |  |
| `--partition-date-end` | Inclusive upper bound of the partition_date window. The wall-clock value is re-interpreted in the Dag's timetable timezone. A date-only value (no time) is treated as local midnight. Accepts the same datetime formats as --end-date. |  |
| `-f`, `--only-failed` | Only failed jobs | flag |
| `-r`, `--only-running` | Only running jobs | flag |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Do not prompt to confirm. Use with care! | flag |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

### airflow dags list-runs

List DAG runs given a DAG id. If state option is given, it will only search for all the dagruns with the given state. If no_backfill option is given, it will filter out all backfill dagruns for given dag id. If start_date is given, it will filter out all the dagruns that were executed before this date. If end_date is given, it will filter out all the dagruns that were executed after this date. If limit is given, it will return only the most recent N runs after filters and sorting are applied.

```text
airflow dags list-runs <dag_id> [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `dag_id` | The id of the dag |  |
| `--no-backfill` | filter all the backfill dagruns given the dag id | flag |
| `--state` `', '.join(dagrun_states)` | Only list the DAG runs corresponding to the state Choices: `dagrun_states`. |  |
| `--limit` | Return a limited number of Dag runs, ordered by most recent run_after first |  |
| `-o`, `--output` `(table, json, yaml, plain)` | Output format. Allowed values: json, yaml, plain, table (default: table) Choices: `('table', 'json', 'yaml', 'plain')`. | `'table'` |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |
| `-s`, `--start-date` | Override start_date. Accepts multiple datetime formats including: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM (ISO 8601), and other formats supported by pendulum.parse() |  |
| `-e`, `--end-date` | Override end_date. Accepts multiple datetime formats including: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM (ISO 8601), and other formats supported by pendulum.parse() |  |

### airflow dags pause

Pause one or more DAGs. This command allows to halt the execution of specified DAGs, disabling further task scheduling. Use `--treat-dag-id-as-regex` to target multiple DAGs by treating the `--dag-id` as a regex pattern.

```text
airflow dags pause <dag_id> [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `dag_id` | The id of the dag |  |
| `--treat-dag-id-as-regex` | if set, dag_id will be treated as regex instead of an exact string | flag |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Do not prompt to confirm. Use with care! | flag |
| `-o`, `--output` `(table, json, yaml, plain)` | Output format. Allowed values: json, yaml, plain, table (default: table) Choices: `('table', 'json', 'yaml', 'plain')`. | `'table'` |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

### airflow dags unpause

Resume one or more DAGs. This command allows to restore the execution of specified DAGs, enabling further task scheduling. Use `--treat-dag-id-as-regex` to target multiple DAGs treating the `--dag-id` as a regex pattern.

```text
airflow dags unpause <dag_id> [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `dag_id` | The id of the dag |  |
| `--treat-dag-id-as-regex` | if set, dag_id will be treated as regex instead of an exact string | flag |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Do not prompt to confirm. Use with care! | flag |
| `-o`, `--output` `(table, json, yaml, plain)` | Output format. Allowed values: json, yaml, plain, table (default: table) Choices: `('table', 'json', 'yaml', 'plain')`. | `'table'` |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

### airflow dags show

The --imgcat option only works in iTerm.

For more information, see: https://www.iterm2.com/documentation-images.html

The --save option saves the result to the indicated file.

The file format is determined by the file extension. For more information about supported format, see: https://www.graphviz.org/doc/info/output.html

If you want to create a PNG file then you should execute the following command:
airflow dags show <DAG_ID> --save output.png

If you want to create a DOT file then you should execute the following command:
airflow dags show <DAG_ID> --save output.dot

```text
airflow dags show <dag_id> [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `dag_id` | The id of the dag |  |
| `-s`, `--save` | Saves the result to the indicated file. |  |
| `--imgcat` | Displays graph using the imgcat tool. | flag |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

### airflow dags test

Execute one single DagRun for a given DAG and logical date.

You can test a DAG in three ways:

1. Using default bundle:
   airflow dags test <DAG_ID>

2. Using a specific bundle if multiple DAG bundles are configured:
   airflow dags test <DAG_ID> --bundle-name <BUNDLE_NAME> (or -B <BUNDLE_NAME>)

3. Using a specific DAG file:
   airflow dags test <DAG_ID> --dagfile-path <PATH> (or -f <PATH>)

The --imgcat-dagrun option only works in iTerm.

For more information, see: https://www.iterm2.com/documentation-images.html

If --save-dagrun is used, then, after completing the backfill, saves the diagram for current DAG Run to the indicated file.
The file format is determined by the file extension. For more information about supported format, see: https://www.graphviz.org/doc/info/output.html

If you want to create a PNG file then you should execute the following command:
airflow dags test <DAG_ID> <LOGICAL_DATE> --save-dagrun output.png

If you want to create a DOT file then you should execute the following command:
airflow dags test <DAG_ID> <LOGICAL_DATE> --save-dagrun output.dot

```text
airflow dags test <dag_id> [logical_date] [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `dag_id` | The id of the dag |  |
| `logical_date` | The logical date of the DAG (optional) |  |
| `-B`, `--bundle-name` | The name of the DAG bundle to use; may be provided more than once | `None` |
| `-f`, `--dagfile-path` | Path to the dag file. Can be absolute or relative to current directory |  |
| `-c`, `--conf` | JSON string that gets pickled into the DagRun's conf attribute |  |
| `--show-dagrun` | After completing the backfill, shows the diagram for current DAG Run.  The diagram is in DOT language | flag |
| `--imgcat-dagrun` | After completing the dag run, prints a diagram on the screen for the current DAG Run using the imgcat tool. | flag |
| `--save-dagrun` | After completing the backfill, saves the diagram for current DAG Run to the indicated file. |  |
| `--use-executor` | Use an executor to test the DAG. By default it runs the DAG without an executor. If set, it uses the executor configured in the environment. | flag |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |
| `--mark-success-pattern` | Don't run task_ids matching the regex <MARK_SUCCESS_PATTERN>, mark them as successful instead. Can be used to skip e.g. dependency check sensors or cleanup steps in local testing. |  |

### airflow db reset

Burn down and rebuild the metadata database

```text
airflow db reset [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Do not prompt to confirm. Use with care! | flag |
| `-s`, `--skip-init` | Only remove tables; do not perform db init. | flag |

### airflow db migrate

Migrate the schema of the metadata database. Create the database if it does not exist To print but not execute commands, use option `--show-sql-only`. If using options `--from-revision` or `--from-version`, you must also use `--show-sql-only`, because if actually *running* migrations, we should only migrate from the *current* Alembic revision.

```text
airflow db migrate [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `-r`, `--to-revision` | (Optional) If provided, only run migrations up to and including this Alembic revision. |  |
| `-n`, `--to-version` | (Optional) The airflow version to upgrade to. Note: must provide either `--to-revision` or `--to-version`. |  |
| `-s`, `--show-sql-only` | Don't actually run migrations; just print out sql scripts for offline migration. Required if using either `--from-revision` or `--from-version`. | flag |
| `--from-revision` | (Optional) If generating sql, may supply a *from* Alembic revision |  |
| `--from-version` | (Optional) If generating sql, may supply a *from* version |  |
| `-m`, `--use-migration-files` | Use migration files to create the database instead of the ORM. This is useful for verifying that the migration files produce the same schema as the ORM models. | flag |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

```text
airflow db downgrade [options]
```

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `-r`, `--to-revision` | The Alembic revision to downgrade to. Note: must provide either `--to-revision` or `--to-version`. |  |
| `-n`, `--to-version` | (Optional) If provided, only run migrations up to this version. |  |
| `-s`, `--show-sql-only` | Don't actually run migrations; just print out sql scripts for offline migration. Required if using either `--from-revision` or `--from-version`. | flag |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Do not prompt to confirm. Use with care! | flag |
| `--from-revision` | (Optional) If generating sql, may supply a *from* Alembic revision |  |

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `-t`, `--tables` | lazy_object_proxy.Proxy(lambda: f"Table names to perform maintenance on (use comma-separated list).\nOptions: {import_string('airflow.cli.commands.db_command.all_tables')}") |  |
| `--dry-run` | Perform a dry run | flag |

| `--error-on-cleanup-failure` | Command will exit with a non-zero exit code if any table cleanup failed. By default errors are suppressed and the command exits 0. | flag |

### airflow partitions clear

Clear the partition_key and partition_date columns on a Dag's DagRuns.
Either --run-id (single run), --partition-key (exact match), or a partition_date range (--start-date/--end-date or --date a~b) is required.
Pass --clear-task-instances to additionally clear the matching DagRuns' task instances so finished runs go back to QUEUED and re-execute.

```text
airflow partitions clear [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `-d`, `--dag-id` | **Required.** The id of the Dag whose DagRun partition fields should be cleared |  |
| `-r`, `--run-id` | Helps to identify this run |  |
| `-s`, `--start-date` | Inclusive lower bound of the partition_date window. |  |
| `-e`, `--end-date` | Inclusive upper bound of the partition_date window. |  |
| `-k`, `--partition-key` | Only clear DagRuns whose `partition_key` equals this exact value |  |
| `--date` | Range expressed as 'a~b' (e.g. '2026-01-01~2026-01-31'); equivalent to --start-date a --end-date b. Mutually exclusive with --start-date / --end-date. |  |
| `--clear-task-instances` | Also clear the matching DagRuns' task instances (resetting finished runs back to QUEUED so they re-execute), in addition to clearing the partition fields. | flag |
| `--dry-run` | Show which DagRuns would be cleared without modifying the database | flag |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

## airflow state-store

Manage task and asset state storage

| Subcommand | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| [`clean`](#airflow-state-store-clean) | Remove expired task state store rows (metastore backend only) |

### airflow state-store clean

Deletes task_state_store rows whose expires_at is in the past, honoring the state_store settings default_retention_days and state_cleanup_batch_size. Currently supports the default metastore backend only; custom (worker-side) backends are skipped. Use --dry-run to preview deletions.

```text
airflow state-store clean [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `--dry-run` | Perform a dry run | flag |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `dag_id` | The id of the dag |  |
| `-t`, `--task-regex` | The regex to filter specific task_ids (optional) |  |
| `-s`, `--start-date` | Override start_date. Accepts multiple datetime formats including: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM (ISO 8601), and other formats supported by pendulum.parse() |  |
| `-e`, `--end-date` | Override end_date. Accepts multiple datetime formats including: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM (ISO 8601), and other formats supported by pendulum.parse() |  |
| `-B`, `--bundle-name` | The name of the DAG bundle to use; may be provided more than once | `None` |
| `-u`, `--upstream` | Include upstream tasks | flag |
| `-d`, `--downstream` | Include downstream tasks | flag |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Do not prompt to confirm. Use with care! | flag |
| `-f`, `--only-failed` | Only failed jobs | flag |
| `-r`, `--only-running` | Only running jobs | flag |
| `-R`, `--dag-regex` | Search dag_id as regex instead of exact string | flag |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

| `--map-index` | Mapped task index | `-1` |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `file` | Import variables from .env, .json, .yaml or .yml file |  |
| `-a`, `--action-on-existing-key` | Action to take if we encounter a variable key that already exists. Choices: `('overwrite', 'fail', 'skip')`. | `'overwrite'` |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

### airflow variables export

All variables can be exported in STDOUT using the following command:
airflow variables export -

```text
airflow variables export <file> [options]
```

| Argument | Description | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `file` | Export all variables to JSON file |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Make logging output more verbose | flag |

## airflow version

Show the version

```text
airflow version
```

No arguments.
